summary: Use accepted main base for ticket-branch push governance

delivery.outcome: Non-default branch pushes validate against their merge base with origin/main while pull-request and review events remain bound to GitHub's exact event base and head SHAs
nonGoals: No change to the adopted governance package or its rules
No change to application, protobuf, profile, or generated bundle contracts
No weakening or removal of required Linux or Windows checks
No public interface, dependency, persistent data, or secret change

architecture.decision: Select governance bases by event semantics in the existing workflow: exact event SHAs for pull-request contexts and a freshly fetched default-branch merge base for other non-default events, implemented symmetrically in Bash and PowerShell
architecture.rollback: Revert the single workflow implementation commit; no application or persistent data migration exists

validation.evidence: Bash and PowerShell non-PR paths fetch the default branch and derive the merge base
Both PR-context paths retain and validate the exact event base SHA
The default-branch changed-file governance path remains unchanged
Host, networkless Docker, workflow syntax, and bounded governance checks pass

commands: Verify protected push and pull-request checks on the published exact head
validation.evidence: Hosted checks must prove the ticket push no longer uses the previous branch commit as base
